items.title: How to Spot a World-Class Designer
items.summary: Julie Zhuo distills a long conversation with Soleio into seven contrasts that separate a great designer from a merely good one — communicating intent over showing artefacts, optimising for the user rather than the portfolio, and treating design decisions as arguments to be won.
items.why: Concrete calibration for what you look for when you hire, promote, or coach at Cuemath — each contrast is a hiring question or a design-review prompt you can put to use next week, not abstract theory.

items.title: Agentic Design Systems: The Complete Guide
items.summary: A written synthesis of five practitioner talks (Brad Frost, Jan Six, Diana Wolosin, and others) on treating a design system less like a Figma library and more like an API that AI agents can read, reason over, and build with — including a self-healing loop that pipes Figma API, CI, and usage signals into automatic drift-fix PRs.
items.why: CueDesign's next question is exactly this — how much of the system needs to be machine-readable, and how do agents actually consume tokens and components? The guide is a shortcut to what leading teams have already tried and where the seams are.

items.title: 7 Questions We Had Going Into Config Leadership Collective
items.summary: Emma Webster reports back from a 1,300-leader gathering at Config, with sharp quotes from design and product heads at OpenAI, Airbnb, and Sephora on what changes in the AI era — pod-based team structures, expertise redefined as judgement rather than execution, and how leaders are actually rolling out AI tooling to their teams.
items.why: Peer benchmark for the design-lead questions you're already sitting with: how to restructure the team around AI-augmented work, and how to hold the craft line while everyone ships faster.

items.title: Tam Festival — visual identity for Florence's first independent publishing fair
items.summary: Edoardo Cantarella and Livia De Magistris build a festival identity around a custom alphabet inspired by Etruscan letterforms and a hand-drawn book-mascot called Zix — a full visual system driven by illustrated typography rather than a wordmark plus palette.
items.why: A working reference for a system anchored on a character plus a custom alphabet, which is the exact shape Cuemath's belts-and-XP world could take when you want a mascot to carry the identity instead of a logo.

items.title: Still magazine — a student issue built entirely around 'sampling'
items.summary: A Central University (Moscow) student magazine that treats typography itself as the sampled material — Antonym paired with CoFo Gothic, laid out with size gradients, staircase glyphs, reversed and circular type. The issue's concept and its layout devices are the same thing.
items.why: Direct precedent for editorial work where the design idea IS the typography — useful territory for Cuemath's long-form and print pieces where the type has to carry the concept, not decorate it.
